title: Files, Paths and Exception Handling
summary: Read and write text files safely, and handle predictable errors using try/except instead of letting the program crash.
objectives: Write lines to a text file with with open(..., "w")
Read a text file back line by line
Catch FileNotFoundError with try/except so a missing file does not crash the program

segments.title: What you will build today
segments.body:
## What you will build today

Until now everything your programs knew was lost the moment they finished. Today you will build a tiny **notes app** that saves its notes to a file called `notes.txt` and reads them back, using `with open(...)` so the file is always closed properly.

Files can be missing, and a careful program expects that. The second half of the lab tries to read a file that does not exist, `missing.txt`, inside a `try/except` block. Instead of crashing with a red error, your program prints a friendly message and carries on to the end.

segments.title: Lab: a notes app that does not crash

lab.title: A notes app that does not crash
lab.objective: Write notes to a file, read them back, and use try/except so a missing file prints a friendly message instead of crashing.
lab.instructions:
The list `notes` already holds three notes.

1. Write every note to `notes.txt`, one per line, using `with open("notes.txt", "w") as f:` and `f.write(note + "\n")`.
2. Open `notes.txt` again for reading and print each line as `Note: <text>` (use `line.strip()` to remove the line break).
3. Try to read `missing.txt` inside a `try:` block. In `except FileNotFoundError:` print `Sorry, missing.txt was not found`. Do not create missing.txt; the point is to handle the error.
4. Keep `print("Done")` as the last line so you can see the program reached the end.

The output must be exactly:

```
Note: Buy milk
Note: Finish Python lab
Note: Call grandma
Sorry, missing.txt was not found
Done
```
lab.constraints: Use with open(...) for every file. Use try/except FileNotFoundError for missing.txt; do not create that file. Keep the file name notes.txt and the list name notes. Print exactly five lines. No input().
lab.starter_code:
# A tiny notes app. There is no input() here: the notes are already in a list.

notes = ["Buy milk", "Finish Python lab", "Call grandma"]

# 1. Save every note to notes.txt, one per line, using:  with open("notes.txt", "w") as f:
# 2. Read notes.txt back with another with open(...) and print each line as:  Note: <text>
# 3. Try to read missing.txt inside try/except FileNotFoundError.
#    If the file is missing, print:  Sorry, missing.txt was not found
#    The program must keep going, not crash.
# 4. Keep the Done line as the last line of output.

print("Done")
hints: Open the file for writing: with open("notes.txt", "w") as f: and inside the block loop over notes and write each one followed by "\n".
Read it back with with open("notes.txt", "r") as f: and for line in f: - print("Note: " + line.strip()). Then put the read of missing.txt inside try: and add except FileNotFoundError: underneath.
The except block prints the friendly message: print("Sorry, missing.txt was not found"). Keep print("Done") as the very last line, outside the try.
